Chapter One: Searching for Meaning in Ancient Instructions
Sometimes, the urge to make sense of life’s big questions leads us down some truly unexpected paths. For one woman, it all started with a simple curiosity—what would happen if she tried to follow every instruction about women in the Bible, as literally as possible, for an entire year? It sounds a bit daunting… maybe even a little out there. But behind that idea was something real—a struggle with faith, tradition, and generations of handed-down expectations. Picture it: a home that looks like any other. There’s laundry piled in baskets, the kitchen table scattered with life’s odds and ends, and the steady hum of daily routines. But beneath it all, there’s this quiet unease. At church, in books, and even over coffee with friends, the phrase “biblical womanhood” keeps popping up. It’s used to describe a pretty specific—and honestly, pretty old-fashioned—set of rules: be gentle, keep quiet, always submit, run the house, raise kids, and above all… don’t question the way things are. But the more she heard these ideas, the less they seemed to fit with real life—or even with the Bible’s own twists and turns. It’s so easy to forget that the Bible’s not just a rulebook. It’s a mix of stories, laws, poems, and letters—written across centuries, in places and cultures that were nothing like ours. Still, a lot of people—especially in some faith communities—hold tight to the thought that there’s one, clear blueprint for how women should live. That clash between ancient words and modern life? That’s what sparked her big experiment: to live out every command and example about women she could find in the Bible, no matter how odd, inconvenient, or uncomfortable. So, where do you even start? She made a list. And it grew fast. Things like: cover your head when you pray, call your husband “master,” avoid gossip, care for those in need, stay silent in church, and even spend time outside the home during your period. Some of these instructions felt familiar—others were just plain jarring. It was a mix of the beautiful and the bewildering, the inspiring and the downright impossible. As the year kicked off, she felt this weird mix of excitement and nerves. There was a sense of adventure, sure, but also a nagging worry—what if this only made things more confusing? What if she ended up with more questions than answers? But you know what? Sometimes, the only way forward is to just start. Those first days were full of small, awkward adjustments. She tied a scarf over her hair before praying, made an effort to speak softly and not interrupt, cooked meals with extra care, and kept the house as tidy as she could. But even these simple acts brought up new questions. Was this really what the Bible wanted? How do you tell the difference between timeless wisdom and ancient customs that just don’t fit today? It didn’t take long to notice: the Bible’s instructions for women aren’t exactly one-size-fits-all. Some passages lift up strong, outspoken women—leaders, prophets, business owners. Others seem to reinforce strict hierarchies and silence. The contradictions were everywhere, and pretty soon, the experiment became less about following rules… and more about wrestling with the text itself. One evening, after a long day of trying—really trying—to submit in every way possible, she sat quietly, feeling exhausted but oddly free. Somehow, in living out these ancient instructions, she was uncovering something deeper—not just about the Bible, but about faith, community, and what it means to be a woman. The year had just begun, but already it was clear: this journey wasn’t about finding easy answers. It was about stepping right into the messiness of real life, real faith, and real questions.
